messages.text: Jones warns England: You were good vs Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent'

metadata.summary: Former England head coach Eddie Jones praised his old side as "very good" as they tore his Japan apart 78-15 on Saturday, but warned the All Blacks will be "violent" against them next week.
metadata.content: Eddie Jones warns England: You were very good against my Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent' next week after Wales loss | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Eddie Jones warns England: You were very good against my Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent' next week after Wales loss Eddie Jones warns England the All Blacks will be 'violent' at Twickenham next week; Will Joseph scored five as England registered 13 tries in huge Nations Championship victory, with Jones' Japan alarmingly inferior; Steve Borthwick admits he now has 'thinking' to do around selection Michael Cantillon Sports Journalist Saturday 14 November 2026 20:41, UK Image: Former England head coach Eddie Jones threw a warning their way ahead of the All Blacks visiting Twickenham next week Former England head coach Eddie Jones praised his old side as "very good" as they tore his Japan apart 78-15 on Saturday, but warned the All Blacks will be "violent" against them next week. Following South Africa's defeat to France in Paris on Friday, victory for New Zealand against Wales in Cardiff would have seen them claim World Rugby's No 1 ranking, and take charge of the Nations Championship southern hemisphere table. Instead, the All Blacks suffered their first defeat to Wales since 1953 in a shock 35-28 loss up against an immense Welsh defensive effort, and next play England at Twickenham next Saturday. messages.text: Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup

metadata.summary: Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea showed his liking for Cheltenham once more and delivered owner JP McManus with his first victory in the prestigious Paddy Power Gold Cup.
metadata.content: Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup Harry Cobden gained his biggest success in his new role with JP McManus as Meetmebythesea stormed to success in the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham, and now bigger targets await Ben Pauling's up-and-coming star Saturday 14 November 2026 16:15, UK Image: Meetmebythesea ridden by Harry Cobden (right) on their way to winning the Paddy Power Gold Cup Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea showed his liking for Cheltenham once more and delivered owner JP McManus with his first victory in the prestigious Paddy Power Gold Cup. Sent off the heavily backed 2-1 favourite on his first run since winning as a novice at the Festival in March, he put in some tremendous leaps on the way round for Harry Cobden. Blueking d'Oroux, having his first run for Dan Skelton, looked the biggest danger after long-time leader Quebecois faded but Meetmebythesea powered away up the hill to win by two and a half lengths to give Cobden a second big victory in two days in the McManus colours.
